name: Pallete
tagline: One prompt. An entire brand identity.
description: Pallete generates complete brand identity systems from a single text prompt. Logos, color palettes, typography pairings, brand guidelines, and social templates — all coherent, all production-ready, all in under sixty seconds. Built for founders who need to look established before they are.
mission:
Starting a company already demands everything you have. You shouldn't also need to become a brand designer. Yet the alternatives are brutal: spend $5K-$30K on an agency (money most founders don't have), DIY something forgettable with free tools, or launch with no visual identity at all and hope nobody notices.

Pallete was founded on a conviction that brand identity is a solvable design problem. Not because branding is simple — it's deeply complex — but because the underlying principles of effective visual identity (contrast, harmony, hierarchy, cultural resonance) are learnable by machines when trained on the right data. We've studied tens of thousands of successful brand systems, from Fortune 500 companies to breakout D2C startups, and distilled the patterns that make identities feel both distinctive and trustworthy.

Our system doesn't generate random aesthetics. You describe your company, your audience, and the feeling you want to evoke, and Pallete produces a coordinated identity system: primary and secondary logos, a curated color palette with accessibility-checked combinations, typography pairings with usage rules, and ready-to-use templates for social media, pitch decks, and business cards. Every element is connected by an internal design logic that ensures coherence.

We're building toward a future where every startup launches with the visual credibility of a company ten times its size. Not because appearances are everything, but because they shape first impressions — and first impressions determine whether someone reads your pitch, clicks your ad, or opens your email.
marketResearch:
The global branding services market exceeds $67B annually, with the subset of logo and identity design representing roughly $12B. AI-powered design tools are projected to capture 15-20% of this market by 2028, driven by SMBs and solo founders who cannot justify traditional agency pricing. Our TAM for automated brand identity generation is approximately $3.8B, with a SAM of $1.2B focused on English-speaking startups and small businesses.

The competitive landscape includes Looka (AI logo maker with 20M+ brands created, but limited to logos and basic brand kits), Brandmark (similar logo-centric approach), and broader design platforms like Canva that offer brand kit features but require manual assembly. Traditional agencies charge $10K-$100K for comprehensive brand identity systems. Pallete occupies the gap: full-system identity generation at software pricing.

Our differentiation is systemic coherence. Competitors generate individual assets; Pallete generates interconnected identity systems where logo, colors, typography, and templates share an internal design logic. Our proprietary Brand Coherence Score evaluates every generated system against 47 criteria spanning legibility, distinctiveness, cultural sensitivity, and cross-medium adaptability.

Early traction shows 73% of users export their generated brand kit within the first session, versus industry-standard conversion rates of 15-20% for design tools. Our GTM leverages startup accelerators (Y Combinator, Techstars partnerships), Product Hunt launches, and integration with company formation platforms like Stripe Atlas and Clerky where brand identity is the natural next step after incorporation.

name: Waveform
description: Waveform reimagines podcast post-production by turning audio into an editable transcript. Cut filler words, rearrange segments, and remove tangents by highlighting and deleting text. The audio follows. Built for podcasters who'd rather tell stories than wrestle with waveforms.
mission:
Podcast editing is stuck in the DAW era. Tools built for music production — multi-track timelines, waveform scrubbing, sample-level precision — are wildly overpowered for what most podcasters actually need: removing ums, tightening transitions, and cutting the segment where the guest's dog started barking.

Waveform started when our founders, both podcasters, realized they spent more time editing than recording. The bottleneck wasn't audio quality or microphone technique — it was the tedious, mechanical process of scrubbing through hours of audio to find and remove the parts that didn't belong. They could identify bad sections instantly by reading a transcript. But translating transcript edits to timeline edits required constant back-and-forth between text and waveform.

So we built the tool that should have existed from the start: an editor where the transcript is the timeline. Select text, delete it, and the audio cuts cleanly. Drag a paragraph to rearrange your episode structure. Highlight filler words across the entire episode and remove them in one click. The audio follows the text, not the other way around.

We're not replacing professional audio engineering. We're eliminating the 90% of podcast editing that's mechanical, repetitive, and doesn't require an audio degree. Our goal is to make weekly publishing sustainable for solo creators and small teams who currently spend six hours editing every hour of content.
marketResearch:
The podcast market has surpassed 4 million active shows globally, with 72% of podcasters editing their own content. The podcast tools and hosting market is valued at $4.1B in 2025, with editing software representing approximately $800M. AI-powered audio editing is the fastest-growing segment at 38% CAGR, driven by solo creators and small production teams seeking efficiency.

Direct competitors include Descript (transcript-based editing pioneer, $100M+ ARR, recently acquired features that dilute podcast focus), Riverside (recording-focused with basic editing), and Adobe Podcast (AI enhancement but limited editing). Traditional DAWs like Audacity and GarageBand remain the default for budget-conscious creators but offer no transcript-based workflow. Waveform differentiates by being podcast-obsessed: every feature is designed for spoken-word content, from smart silence detection to cross-talk handling to show-notes generation.

Our ICP is the weekly podcaster producing 1-4 episodes per month who currently spends 3-6 hours per episode on post-production. This represents roughly 1.8 million creators globally. With an average willingness-to-pay of $19/month, our SOM is approximately $410M annually.

Go-to-market is community-driven: partnerships with podcast hosting platforms (Buzzsprout, Transistor, Podbean), presence in podcasting subreddits and Facebook groups, and a YouTube channel demonstrating real editing workflows. Our free tier (2 hours/month of transcription and editing) converts at 14% to paid plans, with the highest conversion trigger being the filler-word removal feature.

name: Prisma
tagline: 3D assets for games — generated, not modeled.
description: Prisma generates production-quality 3D models, textures, and animations from text descriptions and reference images. Purpose-built for game developers who need dozens of assets fast without sacrificing art direction. From props to characters, Prisma outputs game-engine-ready files with proper topology, UV maps, and LOD variants.
mission:
Game development has a brutal asset bottleneck. A single environment in a modern game can require hundreds of unique 3D models, each needing proper topology, UV unwrapping, texturing, rigging, and LOD optimization. Even experienced 3D artists spend days on a single character model. For indie studios, the math simply doesn't work — you can't ship a visually competitive game when your art pipeline moves at human speed.

Prisma exists to break the asset bottleneck. We're not building a novelty tool that generates impressive-looking renders with broken geometry underneath. We're building a production pipeline that outputs game-engine-ready assets with clean topology, efficient UV layouts, PBR texture sets, and multiple LOD variants. Every model we generate can go straight into Unity or Unreal without manual cleanup.

Our approach is game-art-native. We trained our models on game assets, not general 3D datasets. This means Prisma understands polygon budgets, knows that a background prop needs different topology than a hero character, and generates textures that tile correctly on modular environment pieces. It thinks like a technical artist because we built it with technical artists.

The studio of the future ships great games with small teams. Not because the games are simpler, but because AI handles the production volume while humans focus on art direction, narrative, and the creative decisions that make a game feel authored rather than generated. Prisma is the asset pipeline for that studio.
marketResearch:
The game development tools market is valued at $3.2B in 2025, with 3D asset creation representing the largest subsegment at approximately $1.4B. AI-assisted 3D generation is projected to grow at 42% CAGR through 2029 as game studios seek to reduce the 60-70% of production budgets consumed by art asset creation. The addressable market for game-ready AI asset generation is approximately $2.1B.

Competitors span two categories: general 3D generators (Meshy, Kaedim, Luma AI) that produce impressive visuals but lack game-production optimization, and traditional DCC tools (Blender, Maya, 3ds Max) augmented with AI plugins. No existing solution combines text-to-3D generation with game-engine-ready output including proper topology, LODs, PBR textures, and animation-ready rigging.

Prisma's technical moat is our game-art training data and engine-specific output optimization. Models generated for Unreal include Nanite-optimized meshes; Unity outputs include properly configured prefabs. Our topology is consistently quad-dominant with edge flow suitable for animation, not the triangulated soup that competing tools produce.

Our ICP includes indie studios (2-20 people), mid-size studios needing to accelerate pre-production, and solo developers building ambitious projects. We price per-asset with subscription tiers: Free (10 assets/month), Pro ($39/month, 100 assets), and Studio ($149/month, unlimited with API access). Early traction includes partnerships with three indie studios on Steam's trending list.

name: Inkwell
tagline: Write the story. Let AI draw the panels.
description: Inkwell is an AI-powered comic creation studio where writers craft narratives and the AI generates consistent artwork panel by panel. Maintain character consistency across entire issues, switch between art styles, and export print-ready pages. Comics and graphic novels, from script to shelf, without needing to draw a single line.
mission:
Every writer has a graphic novel trapped inside them. The medium is uniquely powerful — combining visual storytelling with narrative depth in ways that neither prose nor film can match. But the barrier to entry is impossibly high. Creating a single issue requires hundreds of individually drawn, inked, and colored panels with consistent characters across every page. Unless you can draw at a professional level or afford to hire an artist for months, your story stays a script.

Inkwell was built to break that barrier. We believe the creative bottleneck in comics should be storytelling, not illustration skill. Our platform lets writers focus on what they do best — crafting dialogue, pacing scenes, building worlds — while AI handles the visual execution with a level of consistency that previous tools couldn't achieve.

Character consistency is where other AI art tools fail catastrophically for sequential art. A hero who looks different in every panel isn't a character — it's a collage. Inkwell solves this with character locking: define a character once and our system maintains their appearance, proportions, and style across hundreds of panels. Same face. Same build. Same costume details. This isn't trivial — it's the core technical challenge we've spent two years solving.

Our ambition extends beyond making comics easier to make. We want to expand who makes them. The comics industry has been gatekept by illustration ability for a century. Inkwell opens the medium to the millions of writers, worldbuilders, and storytellers who think visually but can't draw — and in doing so, we believe entirely new kinds of stories will emerge.
marketResearch:
The global comic book and graphic novel market is valued at $14.2B in 2025, with digital comics growing at 9.1% CAGR. The adjacent market of webtoons and digital sequential art is exploding — platforms like Webtoon and Tapas collectively reach 180M+ monthly users. The AI creative tools market intersects here at roughly $2.6B, with comic-specific AI tools representing an early but fast-growing $340M segment.

Competitors include general AI image generators (Midjourney, DALL-E) which lack panel consistency, comic-specific tools like ComicAI and Neural Canvas which handle simple strips but not long-form narratives, and traditional digital art tools (Clip Studio Paint, Procreate) which still require drawing skill. Inkwell is unique in combining narrative-aware panel generation with cross-issue character consistency.

Our key differentiator is the Character Persistence Engine — a proprietary system that maintains visual identity across unlimited panels. Combined with panel-aware composition (AI understands comic page layouts, speech bubble placement, and visual flow), Inkwell is the first tool that can produce a 24-page comic issue where characters look consistent from cover to back page.

Target segments include aspiring comic creators (25M+ globally who consume but can't create), indie authors looking to adapt their novels, educators creating visual learning materials, and professional writers prototyping visual narratives before hiring illustrators. Pricing: Free (5 pages/month), Creator ($24/month, 50 pages), and Publisher ($69/month, unlimited pages with print-ready export).

name: Cadence
tagline: Licensed music for creators who actually care about music.
description: Cadence is a music licensing marketplace connecting independent musicians with content creators. Every track is pre-cleared for YouTube, TikTok, podcasts, and commercial use. No copyright strikes, no claim disputes, no royalty surprises. Creators find the perfect track. Musicians earn real money. Everyone's license is clean.
mission:
The music licensing industry is broken from both sides. Creators wade through millions of generic stock tracks, terrified of copyright strikes that can tank a channel overnight. Musicians watch their work get stolen or earn fractions of a cent through streaming while stock music libraries pay flat buyout fees that don't reflect actual usage.

Cadence was founded to fix the transaction, not just the catalog. We built a marketplace where independent artists set their own prices, retain ownership of their masters, and earn usage-based royalties that grow as a creator's content grows. On the other side, creators get instant, unambiguous licenses with automated Content ID whitelisting — no more disputing claims or worrying about monetization being stolen by rights-holders.

Our catalog is curated, not flooded. We reject 70% of submissions to maintain quality parity with custom composition at a fraction of the cost. Every track on Cadence is produced to broadcast standard, properly mastered, and tagged with mood, energy, tempo, and instrumentation metadata that makes discovery genuinely useful rather than keyword roulette.

We believe music licensing should feel like collaboration, not a legal transaction. When a creator finds the perfect track for their video, it should be a moment of creative alignment — not a moment of anxiety about whether they'll get a copyright notice three months later. And when a musician's track scores a viral video, they should share in that success, not receive a one-time $50 buyout.
marketResearch:
The music licensing and sync market is valued at $5.8B globally in 2025, with the creator economy segment (YouTubers, podcasters, social media creators) growing at 28% CAGR. An estimated 50M content creators need licensed music regularly, yet 63% report difficulty finding quality tracks they can afford and trust to be properly cleared.

Competitors include Epidemic Sound ($200M+ ARR, subscription model but limited to their in-house catalog), Artlist (growing but similar closed-catalog approach), Musicbed (premium positioning, high prices), and free/low-cost libraries like Pixabay Music and YouTube's Audio Library (poor quality and limited selection). Cadence differentiates as a two-sided marketplace: open to independent artists while maintaining curation standards, with transparent usage-based pricing rather than all-you-can-eat subscriptions.

Our marketplace model creates a natural moat: more quality artists attract more creators, more usage generates more artist earnings, attracting more artists. We take a 20% platform fee — lower than Spotify's effective cut and dramatically more transparent. Artists on Cadence earn an average of $340/track/month versus $0.003-$0.005 per stream on Spotify.

Our SOM targets mid-tier content creators (10K-1M followers) producing weekly content across YouTube, TikTok, and podcasts, representing approximately $1.4B in annual music licensing spend. GTM strategy combines creator community partnerships, artist referral programs, and integration with major video editing tools (Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut).

name: Moodboard
description: Moodboard is a collaborative visual research platform for design teams. Collect references from anywhere on the web, organize them into spatial canvases with AI-powered clustering, and share living moodboards that stay in sync across your team. Stop drowning in Pinterest boards and Figma frames full of screenshots.
mission:
The visual research phase of design is simultaneously the most important and the most chaotic. Before a single pixel gets pushed, designers spend hours — sometimes days — collecting references, screenshots, color palettes, typography samples, and inspiration from across the web. This research shapes every downstream decision. And yet it lives in the most disorganized places imaginable: browser bookmarks, Pinterest boards, scattered Figma frames, and Slack threads that disappear into the void.

Moodboard was born from watching this chaos repeat across every design team we worked with. The research is critical, but the tools are afterthoughts. Pinterest wasn't built for professional design research. Figma's infinite canvas is a powerful design tool, not a research organizer. And dedicated tools like Eagle or Milanote don't understand visual design well enough to help with organization — they're just folders with thumbnails.

We built Moodboard to be the first tool that actually understands visual research. Our AI analyzes collected references not just by tags or titles, but by visual properties: color palette, composition style, typography approach, texture, and mood. It can cluster your references automatically, suggest related imagery you haven't found yet, and identify the common visual threads across a messy collection of 200 references that your team has been staring at for a week.

Collaborative design research shouldn't be an oxymoron. When a team of four designers is researching a rebrand, they should be able to work in the same visual space, see each other's additions in real-time, and converge on a direction together rather than merging four separate Pinterest boards in a meeting.
marketResearch:
The design collaboration tools market is valued at $7.8B in 2025, with Figma, Miro, and Canva dominating broad collaboration. The niche of visual research and moodboarding tools — including Eagle, Milanote, Pinterest business, and Savee — represents approximately $620M in annual spend. This segment is growing at 22% CAGR driven by remote design teams needing better asynchronous visual communication.

Current solutions fall into three categories: consumer platforms repurposed for professional use (Pinterest — good discovery, terrible organization), general-purpose canvases (Miro, FigJam — lack visual intelligence), and asset management tools (Eagle, Ember — local-first, weak collaboration). No existing tool combines web clipping, AI-powered visual analysis, spatial organization, and real-time team collaboration.

Moodboard's technical differentiator is our Visual DNA engine — a proprietary system that analyzes every collected reference across 23 visual dimensions (color distribution, compositional balance, typographic style, texture density, etc.) and uses these vectors for intelligent clustering, similarity search, and trend identification. This lets design leads ask questions like 'show me the references that share this color energy but have more geometric compositions.'

Our ICP is design teams of 3-15 people at agencies, tech companies, and brand studios. Average contract value is $18/seat/month with team sizes averaging 7 seats. Early adoption is strongest at branding agencies where visual research is billable work. GTM combines Figma community presence, design Twitter/X thought leadership, and partnerships with design education platforms.

faqs.question: Is my visual research private?
faqs.answer: By default, all boards are private to your team. You can share individual boards via link with optional password protection. Enterprise plans include SSO, audit logs, and data residency options.

name: Reel
tagline: Short-form video that doesn't take all day to make.
description: Reel is a browser-based short-form video editor built for speed. Auto-captioning, one-click templates, smart cut detection, and platform-specific export for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. Go from raw footage to published content in minutes, not hours. Designed for creators and social media teams who post daily.
mission:
Short-form video has eaten the internet. TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts — collectively they consume more attention than any other content format. For creators and brands, posting regularly isn't optional; it's survival. But the production workflow is still agonizingly slow. Shoot a video, transfer it to your desktop, open a heavyweight editor, add captions manually frame by frame, export at the right aspect ratio, and upload to three different platforms. For a 60-second video, you easily burn two hours.

Reel exists because the editing tool should match the speed of the format. Short-form video is meant to be quick, raw, and high-volume. The editor should be too. We built everything in the browser — no downloads, no installations, no waiting for imports. Drag in your clip and start editing immediately.

Our killer feature is intelligent auto-captioning with style templates. Captions aren't just accessibility anymore — they're a creative element that defines your content's visual identity. Reel generates word-level accurate captions and lets you style them with animations, highlights, and emoji reactions in a few clicks. The same captioning that takes 45 minutes in Premiere takes 30 seconds in Reel.

We're building the production stack that makes daily posting sustainable. Not by lowering quality, but by eliminating every mechanical step between having footage and having a post. When creation takes minutes instead of hours, creators can actually experiment, iterate, and find what resonates — instead of burning their energy on production busywork.
marketResearch:
The video editing software market is valued at $4.6B in 2025, with the mobile and browser-based segment growing at 31% CAGR. Short-form video tools specifically represent a $1.8B opportunity driven by 200M+ active content creators globally. The average creator spends 6.3 hours per week on video editing, creating massive demand for tools that compress this workflow.

Direct competitors include CapCut (ByteDance's free editor with 400M+ downloads, dominant but primarily mobile), Opus Clip (AI-powered clip extraction from long-form, narrow use case), and traditional editors like Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve (powerful but overkill for short-form). Browser-based competitors like Kapwing and Veed.io are closest but lack the speed-focused UX and intelligent captioning depth that daily creators need.

Reel differentiates on three axes: browser-native speed (no downloads, instant import, sub-second previews), captioning as a first-class creative tool (not an afterthought checkbox), and platform intelligence (we understand TikTok's safe zones, Reels' aspect ratios, and Shorts' metadata requirements, exporting optimized versions for each). Our Smart Cut feature uses transcript analysis to identify and remove dead air, hesitations, and off-topic tangents automatically.

Our ICP spans solo creators posting 5+ times per week, social media teams at D2C brands, and agency teams managing multiple client accounts. Pricing is freemium: Free (3 exports/month with watermark), Pro ($14/month, unlimited exports, all caption styles), and Team ($29/seat/month, brand kits, shared templates, approval workflows).

name: Typecast
tagline: Your voice. Your audiobook. No studio required.
description: Typecast creates studio-quality AI voice clones for audiobook narration. Record 30 minutes of your voice, and Typecast generates a narrator that sounds like you — with natural pacing, emotional range, and consistent delivery across an entire book. Authors and publishers produce professional audiobooks at a fraction of traditional recording costs.
mission:
Only 7% of published books have an audiobook edition. Not because demand is low — audiobook revenue grew 25% last year — but because production is prohibitively expensive. A professional narrator charges $200-$400 per finished hour. A 10-hour audiobook costs $2,000-$4,000 in narrator fees alone, plus studio time, editing, and mastering. For indie authors earning $500-$2,000 per title, the math doesn't work.

Typecast was built to democratize audiobook production. We don't use generic text-to-speech voices that sound robotic and lifeless. We clone the author's own voice — or let them choose from a library of professional narrator voices — and produce narration with natural pacing, emotional inflection, and the subtle prosodic variations that make audiobooks engaging rather than exhausting to listen to.

The technical challenge is enormous. Audiobook narration isn't just reading text aloud. It's performance. A great narrator handles dialogue with distinct character voices, adjusts pacing for tension and release, and maintains consistency across 80,000+ words. Our models are trained specifically for long-form narration, understanding paragraph-level context to deliver appropriate emotional tone, and maintaining voice stability across chapters that might take 12+ hours to render.

We see a future where every book has an audiobook. Where indie authors can reach the 45% of book consumers who prefer audio. Where publishers can produce audiobook editions simultaneously with print and digital, not months or years later. Typecast is the production engine that makes that future economically viable.
marketResearch:
The global audiobook market reached $7.8B in 2025 and is projected to hit $15B by 2030 at 14% CAGR. Yet supply is severely constrained: only 7% of the 4M+ books published annually get audiobook editions. The AI voice technology market, valued at $4.2B, is converging with audiobook production to create a new category worth an estimated $1.6B by 2028.

Competitors include ElevenLabs (powerful voice cloning but general-purpose, not optimized for long-form narration), Google and Amazon's TTS services (adequate for navigation, inadequate for storytelling), DeepZen (audiobook-focused but limited voice variety and high pricing), and Apple's AI narration (limited to Apple Books, restricted voice options). Typecast differentiates by combining author voice cloning with narration-specific training that handles dialogue, pacing, and emotional range at book length.

Our core technical moat is long-form coherence. Competitors produce impressive 30-second samples that degrade over minutes. Typecast maintains voice quality, emotional consistency, and prosodic naturalness across 10+ hour narrations. Our Chapter Context Engine reads ahead to understand narrative arc and adjusts delivery accordingly — quieter for intimate scenes, faster for action sequences, distinct voices for different characters.

Primary segments include indie authors (2.3M self-published titles annually, $29/book pricing), small publishers (500-5,000 titles/year, volume licensing), and corporate/educational publishers needing training materials and course narration. GTM starts with integrations into self-publishing platforms (KDP, IngramSpark, Draft2Digital) where authors are already producing books without audiobook editions.

name: Easel
tagline: Digital paint that feels like the real thing.
description: Easel is a digital painting application built around natural brush physics. Real bristle simulation, paint mixing that behaves like actual pigment, and canvas textures you can feel through your stylus. No layers palette, no vector tools, no feature bloat — just the purest digital painting experience for artists who care about the craft.
mission:
Digital painting tools have spent thirty years adding features and forgetting what painting actually feels like. Photoshop has 300+ brushes but none that behave like a real sable round. Procreate is elegant but its brushes are stamp-based simulations. Corel Painter comes closest but it's buried under decades of enterprise feature creep. The tools optimized for painters — actual painters — don't exist.

Easel started from a radically simple premise: what if we built a painting app for people who love painting? Not photo manipulation, not graphic design, not illustration workflows — painting. The act of loading a brush with color, touching it to a textured surface, and watching the pigment spread, thin, and blend in ways that respond to pressure, angle, and speed.

Our brush engine simulates individual bristles interacting with canvas texture at the fiber level. When you press harder, the bristles splay. When paint runs low, the stroke dries out naturally. When two wet colors meet, they mix the way real pigments do — following subtractive color theory, not additive RGB blending. The result is a painting experience that makes artists forget they're using a screen.

We deliberately left features out. No layers palette (paint over it or scrape it off, like real paint). No selection tools. No filters. Easel is an opinionated tool that says: if you want to paint, we'll give you the best digital painting experience ever built. If you want to do graphic design, use a graphic design tool. This focus lets us pour all of our engineering into the one thing that matters — how the brush feels on the canvas.
marketResearch:
The digital art software market is valued at $3.9B in 2025, with painting-specific applications representing approximately $680M. The growing overlap between fine art and digital tools is driven by 15M+ digital artists globally, with the traditional/fine art crossover segment growing at 18% CAGR as established painters explore digital workflows and digital artists seek more natural, tactile experiences.

Direct competitors include Procreate ($12.8M annual revenue, dominant on iPad but stamp-based brushes), Corel Painter ($200+ perpetual license, powerful but complex and aging), Adobe Fresco (free tier but shallow brush physics, part of Adobe ecosystem), and Rebelle (closest in natural media simulation but limited platform support and rough UX). Easel occupies a unique position: production-grade brush physics with the simplicity of a focused, modern app.

Our technical moat is the Bristle Physics Engine — a real-time simulation of individual brush fibers interacting with canvas surface topology. Unlike stamp-based engines (which tile a pre-drawn brush shape), our engine calculates bristle flex, paint load, and surface friction on every frame. This produces brush behavior that traditional painters describe as 'the first digital tool that doesn't feel like a computer.'

Target segments include traditional artists transitioning to digital (5M+), digital artists seeking natural media aesthetics, art educators teaching painting fundamentals, and concept artists who prefer a painterly workflow. Pricing: $39.99 one-time purchase (iPad/desktop), with optional brush pack and canvas texture subscriptions at $4.99/month. Our App Store rating is 4.9/5 with particular praise for brush feel.

name: Montage
tagline: Remote video teams, one seamless timeline.
description: Montage is a video collaboration platform for distributed production teams. Editors, directors, colorists, and sound designers work on the same project simultaneously from anywhere. Real-time timeline sync, frame-accurate commenting, version branching, and role-based workflows replace the fragmented mess of shared drives and review links.
mission:
Video production went remote but the tools didn't follow. Post-production workflows still assume everyone is in the same edit suite. Editors upload cuts to Frame.io for review. Directors leave timecoded comments that get manually translated back into timeline edits. Colorists receive exported XMLs that don't round-trip cleanly. Sound designers work with stems that are already outdated by the time they receive them. The entire process is a chain of exports, uploads, downloads, and version conflicts.

Montage replaces that chain with a single, synchronized workspace. When an editor makes a cut, the director sees it in real-time. When a colorist adjusts a grade, it's immediately visible in the editor's timeline. When a sound designer adds a mix, everyone hears it. No exports. No uploads. No 'which version is current?' The project is one living thing that the whole team shapes together.

We built this because our founding team spent a decade in post-production, and the pandemic made the existing workflow's fragility impossible to ignore. Remote editors wasted 30% of their time on file management. Review cycles that should take hours stretched into days of async back-and-forth. Version control was a spreadsheet and a prayer. The creative work suffered because the logistics consumed everyone's energy.

Montage is the infrastructure layer that makes distributed video production feel like being in the same room. Not through video calls and screen shares, but through a shared creative workspace where every team member's contribution is immediately integrated into the living project.
marketResearch:
The video post-production software market is valued at $4.1B in 2025, with cloud-based and collaborative solutions growing at 26% CAGR. Remote and hybrid production is now the default for 68% of production companies post-pandemic. The specific market for video collaboration tools — review, approval, and team workflow — is approximately $1.3B, dominated by Frame.io (acquired by Adobe) with significant greenfield opportunity in real-time collaborative editing.

The competitive landscape includes Frame.io (strong review and approval but not real-time editing), Evercast (screen sharing for remote sessions, not true collaboration), LucidLink (cloud storage that mimics local drives, solves file access but not workflow), and traditional NLEs (Premiere, Resolve, Avid) that are adding cloud features but remain fundamentally single-editor tools. No existing platform offers true simultaneous multi-role editing on a shared timeline.

Montage's technical moat is our Conflict-Free Replicated Timeline (CRDT-based) that allows multiple editors to work on the same sequence without merge conflicts. Combined with role-based access (editors can cut, colorists can grade, sound designers can mix — each in their lane without stepping on each other), Montage enables genuine real-time collaboration rather than turn-taking.

Our ICP includes independent production studios (15-50 person teams), advertising agencies with video departments, corporate video teams at large enterprises, and YouTube production teams with distributed editors. Pricing starts at $49/seat/month for teams, with enterprise plans including dedicated rendering infrastructure, compliance features, and custom integrations. Early traction includes pilots with two major advertising agencies and a Netflix-contracted post house.
